doc: bsv-low #499: the D1 ceilings of the budget tier (docs/D1-BUDGETS.md). Each ceiling is the figure measured on the fixture D1 (b1ad9a1 plus lane 499, 2026-10-07, identical at 300 and 1200 strangers) plus the margin below; raise one only with a new measurement and its reason in the doc.
margin: reads: measured x 1.5 rounded up, at least measured + 4; writes: measured + 2, and a route that measured 0 writes keeps 0 (a read that starts writing reds); stmts: measured + 2

owed-first-read.route: /owed?identity=A: the first read (the compute on read and its write); A's swept hop's sweep is a DURABLE spender with a proofmined: latch, so the recompute makes the latch range read (bsv-low #693 fold-2)

spent-any-20.route: /spent-any?outpoints=<20 outpoints>: twenty fresh probe memos naming twenty of the fleet's proven transactions as spenders, no confirmed word, so every row is a known spend and the one index-proof read (hopsweep::sweep_proofs_sql, a PK seek, 20 spenders) confirms each (bsv-low #723)

submit-admit-1.route: /submit: an operator historical-tx-no-spv submit admitting one tm_collected output

record-potparty-filing.route: /record?kind=potparty: a signed stranger filing naming A's pot; all inline filing reads and marks

pot-changed-hook-1.route: /internal/pot-changed: B's pot, one outpoint, no decoded params, its two marker-named seats marked stale (E649 L4: the required read, the marker arms one batch each, ONE write batch of the stale marks and the outpoint's parked wake-up (H1); no walk, no relay call on the answer path; the park batch reads the table's room ONCE, after its parks (N6, fold-3: the counter, then the guard and the room-making delete, each at limit 0 under the ceiling), one LIMITed scan of the parked table, at most 2,048 rows (E649 L4 N3; 126 parked rows here, so the largest statement is 127), and takes its tokens from the one-row counter (N1))

pot-changed-hook-decoded-8.route: /internal/pot-changed: A's eight decoded pots, one latched seat each (E649 L4 M1, the decoded maximum body: one required batch of 8, the seat markers' batch, ONE write batch of 16 parked wake-ups; no marker arm is read; the park batch reads the table's room ONCE, after its parks (N6, fold-3: the counter, then the guard and the room-making delete, each at limit 0 under the ceiling), one LIMITed scan of the parked table, at most 2,048 rows (E649 L4 N3; 126 parked rows here, so the largest statement is 127), and takes its tokens from the one-row counter (N1))

pot-changed-hook-marker.route: /internal/pot-changed: the fixture's undecoded pot whose party and refund-backup markers name five identities with owed-state rows (E649 L4 M1, the marker fallback: the required read, three arm batches, ONE write batch of five stale marks and one park; the park batch reads the table's room ONCE, after its parks (N6, fold-3: the counter, then the guard and the room-making delete, each at limit 0 under the ceiling), one LIMITed scan of the parked table, at most 2,048 rows (E649 L4 N3; 126 parked rows here, so the largest statement is 127), and takes its tokens from the one-row counter (N1))

pot-changed-hook-8x19.route: /internal/pot-changed: seven decoded pots with two latched seats each and the marker pot naming five, 19 identities each with an owed-state row (E649 L4 M1, the review's H2 body: required batch of 8, seat markers, three arm batches over the one marker outpoint, ONE write batch of 5 stale marks and 22 parks; the park batch reads the table's room ONCE, after its parks (N6, fold-3: the counter, then the guard and the room-making delete, each at limit 0 under the ceiling), one LIMITed scan of the parked table, at most 2,048 rows (E649 L4 N3; 126 parked rows here, so the largest statement is 127), and takes its tokens from the one-row counter (N1))

pot-announce-drain-backlog.route: /internal/pot-announce-drain: the first pass over the fixture's backlog of 120 due and 6 exhausted parked wake-ups (E649 L4 N3: four rounds, each the due read, LIMIT 24, then ONE write batch of its 24 settles; the first round's batch also ages out (LIMIT 50) and sweeps (LIMIT 50))

pot-announce-drain.route: /internal/pot-announce-drain: the second pass, over the 24 due wake-ups the backlog pass left (E649 L4 H1, N3: the due read, LIMIT 24, ONE write batch of 24 settles, the age-out and the sweep; the round was full, so one more due read finds none)

pot-changed-hook-full-refused.route: /internal/pot-changed: eight new rooms at a FULL table of 2,048 live rows none of which may be displaced (E649 L4 N6, fold-3: the batch's eight parks, the counter's one LIMITed scan of at most 2,056 rows, the guard over the rows that may make room (none), which faults and rolls the batch back; answered 503. D1 answers a FAILED batch with no meta, so the ledger counts the reads before it only. NOT the refusal's total (N10, the third delta review): the batch's counter scan (up to 2,056 rows) and its guard, which with no eligible row visits EVERY row (2,059 by the review's D1 binding), are real and unreported; the total is about 16 + 2,057 + 2,059 = 4,132 rows, stated in docs/D1-BUDGETS.md, each scan bounded by the tail scenario's measured maxReads)

pot-changed-hook-full-room-tail.route: /internal/pot-changed: eight fresh rooms at a FULL table whose eight exhausted rows sit at the TAIL of the scan order (E649 L4 N10, the third delta review: the guard's LIMIT counts ELIGIBLE rows, not rows visited, so it visits the whole table to find them; the counter's scan and the delete's ORDER BY as in full-room). The worst placement of the room-making arm

pot-changed-hook-full-room.route: /internal/pot-changed: the same eight rooms once eight rows are exhausted (E649 L4 N6, fold-3: eight parks, the counter's scan, the guard reading the eight exhausted rows, the room-making delete of them, ordered, RETURNING)

health-invariants.route: /health/invariants: the overlay's invariants read, the second of two answers 250 ms apart (the harness cells' settle shape, bsv-low #838); its reads issued in one join, its rows-read bump after the answer (writes 0 at the answer). settleCeilingMs: the two answers' wall time on the fixture, measured 325 ms (2026-10-22, LANE_BASE 38380), held far under the harness's 20 s settle; not a production latency (local D1 has no queue).

censusKey: the d1Budget route a production census holds against this ceiling (advisory there: production rows are not the fixture's); null = the route's maximum is another scenario's

d1RowsReadPerDay.doc: NS-COST-BAR-1 (the owner's cost word of 2026-10-18: no self-inflicted Cloudflare bill): the DAILY rows-read budget of LOW's own D1 databases per environment, judged by the daily census (scripts/d1-census.py, bsv-low docs/audit/D1-CENSUS-*-24H-*.md) and by the deltas of /health/invariants.d1RowsRead (the overlay's d1_rows_read_<family>_total counters) over a day. Scope: every LOW database of the environment (prod: low-overlay-db, low-relay-prod; beta: low-overlay-db-beta, low-identity-db-beta, low-identity-resolver-db-beta, low-relay-beta); the keeper's rust-chaintracks is FOREIGN, reported beside the budget and never inside it (its count of headers is the keeper's ask, docs/D1-BUDGETS.md). Raise a figure only with a new census and its reason in docs/D1-BUDGETS.md.
d1RowsReadPerDay.rule: a day's rows over the environment's budget is RED; beside it the census's own 3x rule stands unchanged (a statement tag whose rows per query exceed 3x the previous loop's committed table is RED at the fold, bsv-low invariants.rules.json d1_census, floor 100 rows).

prod.why: the 24-hour census of 2026-10-17 (2026-10-17T00:03:52Z to 2026-10-18T00:03:52Z) read 8.9 M rows a day on low-overlay-db in its 60 listed tags; the statements PR #86 (#643, #644, #645) and NS-COST-BAR-1 bound account for 5.1 M of them, leaving about 3.8 M plus the 105 unlisted tags. 20 M is about 5x that remainder: the census's own 3x margin over it with room for the unlisted tail; and well under the 73 M the environment read that day, 61 M of it the keeper's count of headers.

beta.why: the same census read 98.5 M rows a day on low-overlay-db-beta (60 listed tags), 88.8 M of them in the statements PR #86 and NS-COST-BAR-1 bound, leaving about 9.7 M, plus 6.4 M on low-identity-db-beta and 0.6 M on the resolver's: about 16.7 M. 60 M is about 3.5x that (the census's 3x margin and the fleet's beta load, which runs ahead of prod), and half the 122 M the environment read that day.

doorAnswer.doc: bsv-low #838 (FIX-838): the broadcast-gated /submit answers inside the harness's 20 s settle (the door's contract, never raised). The arm stops WAITING on its engine write at answerDeadlineMs from the arm's start (the write goes on in ctx.wait_until), defers the submission as NL-6c does (the 202 and its poll; the job's queue message delayed jobDelaySecs, past the platform's 30 s end of that wait_until) and waits at most deferAtRestCapMs to put it at rest: ceilingMs = answerDeadlineMs + deferAtRestCapMs. Pinned natively over a virtual clock (`ef_deferred::fix838`), not driven by this tier: the gated arm needs Arcade and its background reaches mainnet hosts, which the tier's loopback seal refuses. measured: loop 44 (full-2026-10-22_15-50-41, 33 pairs, beta, 15:49Z to 17:19Z), server-side from the low-overlay-beta logs (694 gated answers) and the client's network leg from 116 harness submits matched to them (docs/audit/FIX-838-door-latency-2026-10-22.md).
